R/O C-3/2 vs The State (Govt. Of Nct Of Delhi) on 10 August,
2016
 1
 In The Court Of Sh. Rakesh Pandit,
 Asj-01, New Delhi District, Patiala House Courts,
 New Delhi
Case Id No. 02403R0184872015
Ca No. 8503/16

Satish Kumar Garg
S/o Sh. Baburam Garg
M/s Garg General Stores,
Shop no. 8, C-6, Dda Market,
Yamuna Vihar, Delhi-110053.
R/o C-3/2, Yamuna Vihar,
Delhi-110053.

....Appellant
 Vs.
The State (Govt. Of Nct of Delhi)
Through Commissioner of Food Safety,
Mayur Bhawan, Connaught Circus,
New Delhi.
.... Respondent
Date of receiving of Appeal : 23.09.2015  Date of arguments : 15.07.2016

Date of judgment : 10.08.2016  JUDGMENT 1 B y t h i s j u d g m e n t I w i l l d i s p o s e o f a p p e a l u / s e c . 3 7 4  Satish Kumar Garg Vs. State Cr.PC. filed on behalf of convict Satish Kumar Garg against the judgment dated 08.09.2015 and order on sentence dated 14.09.2015 passed by Sh.
Gaurav Rao, Ld. ACMM-II, Patiala House Court, New Delhi.

2 The brief facts of the case as per record and from trial court record are that accused is running an establishment namely M/s Garg General Store, Shop no. 8, C-6, DDA Market, Yamuna Vihar,
Delhi-110053.
On 19.05.2003 at about 6.30 p.m. Food Inspector Sh. Suniti Kumar Gupta visited the said place and purchased 1500 grams of "Dal Masoor" from accused.

FI was accompanied with R/O C-3/2 vs The State (Govt. Of Nct Of Delhi) on 10 August, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/2826006/
1 SDM/LHA Sh. T. S. Mutti.
The said Dal Masoor was purchased for the purposes of analysis under PFA Act.
The same sample was divided into three parts, packed as per Rules of PFA.
Panchanama was prepared.
One sample was sent for analysis to Public Analyst.

As per the report of Analyst,
sample did not confirm to the standard because "The sample is adulterated because it is coloured with synthetic colouring matter viz. Sunset Yellow FCF."
3 As the sample was failed, prosecution was launched by Food Inspector by filing complaint dated 31.10.2003 with the court.
Accused was summoned.
He has exercised his right u/sec.13(2) PFA Act to get the sample analyzed by CFL.

CFL opined that "I am of the opinion that the sample bearing no.
52/LHA/4000 does Satish Kumar Garg Vs. State not conform to the stands of Split Pulse (Dal) Masoor as per PFA Rules, 1955 (synthetic colour Sunset Yellow FCF and Carmoisine detected)."
4

Charge was framed against accused u/sec.2(ia) (a) (j)
(m) read with sec.7 of PFA Act, 1954 punishable u/sec.16(1A) of PFA Act.

5 After trial, vide judgment dated 08.09.2015 accused was convicted for offence u/sec.16(1A) of PFA Act and vide order on sentence dated 14.09.2015, accused was directed to undergo simple imprisonment for a period of 18 months and fine of Rs.10,000/- and in default of payment of fine SI of 30 days.

6 In this appeal, the accused has assailed the judgment on the following grounds:-
(i) Non-compliance of Sec.10(7) of PFA Act and Rule i.e. independent witnesses were not joined.

(ii) Non-compliance of Rule 14 of PFA Rules i.e. the bottles, jhawa, polythene were not made clean and dried at the spot by the food inspector or any other official.
(iii) There is variation in the reports of PA and CFL and the benefit goes in favour of accused/appellant.
7
No reply was filed by respondent/state and the matter was argued orally.
8 I h a v e g o n e t h r o u g h t h e r e c o r d , T r i a l C o u r t r e c o r d a n d
Satish Kumar Garg Vs. State have heard the submissions of Ld. counsel for appellant and Ld. SPP for State.
9 It is argued by counsel for appellant that no public witness was present in the proceedings nor efforts were made to join any public witnesses.
As far as this argument is concerned, the same argument was raised before the Ld. Trial Court.
The same was dealt by the trial court from para 20 to 26 of the judgment.

As far as opinion/finding of the trial court regarding this argument is concerned, I do not find any infirmity in those findings and the same are upheld and the arguments R/O C-3/2 vs The State (Govt. Of Nct Of Delhi) on 10 August, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/2826006/
2 regarding this fact
does not find any force and thus rejected.
10 It is further stated that there is variation in the report of PA and CFL and due to that reason benefit goes in favour of the accused.
This line of argument was done before the trial court and was dealt in para 57 to 91 of the judgment.
I do not want to differ from the reasoning given by the trial court and thus the same is upheld.
11 It is further argued that compliance u/sec.14 PFA Rules was not proved on record by the prosecution.
It is stated that witnesses are deposing differently with respect to the cleanliness of jhaba etc.
It is further stated that it was the duty of the prosecution to prove these facts.
It is further stated that there are Satish Kumar Garg Vs. State discrepancies in the testimony of various witnesses.
These arguments were also addressed before the trial court.

The relevant part of the judgment dealing with these arguments are from para 27 to 46 of the judgment and further argued that there are contradictions/discrepancies in the statement of witnesses regarding the cleanliness of the jhaba etc. 12

As far as the discrepancies are concerned, the court has given its opinion on the basis that even if there are minor discrepancies, if those does not goes to the root and are not substantial, it does not effect the case of the prosecution.
As far as the arguments in this regard is concerned, the law discussed by the trial court is correct and the same is self explanatory.
However, as far as the analysis of facts are concerned, to my opinion, the same requires some more elaboration.
13 As far as Rule 14 of PFA Rules are concerned, it spells out that the FI shall use dry bottles or containers for the purposes of sampling.

However, this fact was elaborated further by Hon. Supreme Court in Varghese Vs. Food, 1989 (II) Prevention of Food Adulteration Cases, 236 stating that "it must be the endeavour of the FI to use clean and dry implements in sampling the articles of food.

entities.text: Varghese Vs. Food, 1989 (II) Prevention of Food Adulteration Cases, 236
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: If unhygienic methods are adopted, it will effect the result of analysis.
So, the Hon. Supreme Court use the Satish Kumar Garg Vs. State word "implements" instead of only "dry and clean bottles/containers".
Similarly, in other judgments, i.e. State of Haryana Vs. Kishan Kumar CLT 559, it was observed that the prosecution had not stated that the "weighing scale" was clean.

entities.text: State of Haryana Vs. Kishan Kumar CLT 559
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Similarly, in other judgments, like Sardar Mal Jain, 1996 (2) Prevention of Food Adulteration Cases,
203, it was stated that the newspaper on which the Barfi was weighed was not clean.

entities.text:
Sardar Mal Jain, 1996 (2) Prevention of Food Adulteration Cases,
203
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Similarly, in Shashi Kant Vs. State of UP, 1983 (1) Prevention of Food Adulteration Cases 90, it was observed that the "bhagona" was not proved to be clean and dry.

entities.text: Shashi Kant Vs. State of UP, 1983 (1) Prevention of Food Adulteration Cases 90
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Similarly, in 2008 (3) RCR (Criminal) 422 Rajinder Kumar Vs. State of Haryana (Punjab and Haryana), it was held by the court that when an envelop is used for weighing the sample commodity, the same must be proved as clean and free from any impurity.

entities.text: 2008 (3) RCR (Criminal) 422 Rajinder Kumar Vs. State of Haryana (Punjab and Haryana)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 14 So, accordingly, it can be said that the law which can be crystallized from various judgments of Hon. High Courts as well as Hon. Supreme Court is that if in evidence, the prosecution states that the sample commodity had touched a surface of an "implement", it is the duty of the prosecution to prove beyond reasonable doubt that the said implement was clean and dry and thus could not have added any impurity to the sample.

However, it is not the law that the FI shall spell out on which s u r f a c e s t h e s a m p l e c o m m o d i t y h a d t o u c h e d w h i l e s a m p l i n g . H o w e v e r , i f h e R/O C-3/2 vs The State (Govt. Of Nct Of Delhi) on 10 August, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/2826006/
3  Satish Kumar Garg Vs. State chooses to spell out the implements/surfaces with which the sample commodity came into contact/touch, the same must be proved as clean and dry.
15 In this case, PW1 (cross-examination dated 12.01.2010) had deposed that "Dal was weighed after putting on clean and dry brown sheet".

However, PW4 (cross-examination dated 10.09.2013)
deposed that "the Dal was weighed on simple weighing pan by putting it in a polythene.
The polythene was available in the shop of the accused."
16 So, according to these two witnesses, there are contradictions in their statements regarding the surface it touched before being weighed.
One said that it was a clean and dry surface of a brown paper.
Other witness stated that it was the polythene.
However, this witness has not deposed anything about cleanliness and dryness of polythene.
17 This contradictions goes in favour of accused/appellant.
Further there are two versions i.e. the sample commodity touched a clean and dry surface OR it touched the surface which was not proved as to whether it was clean or dry.
18 When there are two facts on record, the fact favourable to accused is to be accepted.
So, in these circumstances, the fact that the sample commodity was weighed after putting it in  Satish Kumar Garg Vs. State polythene bag is to be taken.

entities.text: Satish Kumar Garg Vs. State polythene bag
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Now, nowhere it is deposed by any witness that the said polythene bag was clean and dry and free from any colour.
19 So, in these circumstances, there is no proper compliance of Rule 14 PFA Rules.
The benefit goes in favour of appellant/convict.
20 So, the judgment and order on sentence of the trial court is reversed.
21 Accused Satish Kumar Garg is acquitted of the charges u/sec.16(1A) read with sec.7 of PFA Act.
22 Bail Bond u/sec.437A Cr.P.C. furnished.
Accepted for six months.
23 TCR be sent back with copy of the order.
24 File of appeal be consigned to Record Room.
ANNOUNCED In the open Court (RAKESH PANDIT) today i.e. 10.08.2016 ASJ-01/
